title: Intraoral high-frequency sonography for imaging periodontal soft tissue changes around the tooth in patients with oral lichen planus - A single-center cross-sectional study
summary:
The diagnosis of oral lichen planus (OLP) is currently based primarily on clinical examination and histopathological analysis of tissue samples. As a non-invasive procedure, intraorally applied high-frequency sonography offers the potential to complement this diagnostic procedure in a low-risk and patient-friendly manner. Using sonographic B-mode imaging, both the epithelial thickness and the dimensional characteristics of the subepithelial connective tissue can be recorded on the gingival soft tissue architecture of the tooth. In addition, a hypoechoic boundary layer can be defined between the hyperechoic epithelium and the underlying connective tissue, which morphologically corresponds to the interlocking rete ridges and connective tissue papillae of the epithelial junction zone. Sonographic dimensional measurements and the analysis of potential changes in echogenicity could provide diagnostically relevant information about structural tissue changes. In addition, functional ultrasound diagnostics enables a dynamic assessment of the gingival tissue perfusion by measuring blood flow velocity and intensity. The visualization of vascular activity is particularly important for the early detection of active inflammatory processes.
The aim of this cross-sectional study is to evaluate whether intraorally applied high-frequency sonography of the periodontal soft tissue on the tooth provides sufficiently differentiating features to distinguish between clinically healthy gingiva and OLP. In the long term, the knowledge gained could contribute to the development of a non-invasive, reproducible diagnostic method and reduce the need for diagnostic biopsies in selected clinical situations.
